subject.title: fix(workboard): separate orchestration from hard dependencies

question: Should Workboard change the default decomposition contract for existing callers and automatically remove ambiguous legacy dependency links, or should orchestration remain explicit until a safe upgrade path is approved?
rationale: The new mode changes persisted relationship semantics and the old data model has no field that records whether a reciprocal link was intentionally hard, so code review cannot infer the intended upgrade policy.

options.title: Preserve existing default
options.body: Keep omitted decompositionMode compatible with the prior hard-link behavior, make orchestration explicit, and limit repair to unambiguous records.

options.title: Adopt orchestration by default
options.body: Approve the behavior change only with release-visible upgrade guidance, a non-destructive legacy repair flow, and proof for both fresh and upgraded databases.

options.title: Pause the migration portion
options.body: Land no automatic repair until the persisted-state intent can be distinguished or users can confirm each candidate.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing default
recommendation.body: Keep omitted decompositionMode compatible with the prior hard-link behavior, make orchestration explicit, and limit repair to unambiguous records.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the most direct context on the proposed Workboard behavior, though a current-main ownership history pass is still needed before final routing.
